note: Count<Derived>, Pixels and the empty RenderQuality. **The tree is build/debug and not build/relwithdebinfo, which every earlier pass used, and the reason is the subject of the task.** Count's wraparound guard has two halves: a call to a function that is not constexpr, which refuses the expression while the compiler evaluates it and so fires in either tree, and an ORBSIM_EXPECTS beside it, which exists only where NDEBUG is not defined. Run in relwithdebinfo, every mutant that only loosens the run-time half survives -- not because the suite has a hole but because the thing being mutated is not there. Debug is the tree where both halves exist, and the compile-time half is unaffected by the choice. Most of these therefore die at compile time and name the assertion that fired. One mutant is a declared survivor and it is the honest one: making the guard's function constexpr-callable in the *run-time* sense changes nothing any test can see, because every wraparound this suite provokes is provoked at compile time and nothing in the project runs one at run time and watches it abort. Closing that needs a death test -- a separate executable that must abort, and only in Debug -- which is a new CTest target and the owner's decision, not this task's.

mutants.why: It survives *this harness*, and no longer survives the suite. The property is checked by the CTest entry count_wraparound_aborts, which this harness structurally cannot run: the probe's success is a non-zero exit -- the assertion firing -- and run_mutant reads any non-zero exit as a kill, so listing it here would report every mutant as caught. Removing the ORBSIM_EXPECTS makes the probe return 1 instead of aborting with 3, which cmake/VerifyCountWraparound.cmake calls a failure and this file cannot. Teaching mutate.py an inverted expectation would close the gap and is the owner's call, not this task's.
